title: Laboratory response to an infant with suspected measles vaccine associated fever and rash in Sri Lanka.
ehr_evidence: This single center, laboratory-based case investigation was carried out in NML, Department of Virology at MRI, SL. Data sharing not applicable to this article as no datasets were generated or analyzed during the current study.
summary: A single-case laboratory investigation describing the diagnosis of a vaccine-associated measles-like illness in a 9-month-old immunocompetent boy in Sri Lanka following MMR vaccination.
key_findings: Measles vaccine-type A (Edmonson-strain) virus was detected by sequencing in a throat swab collected at day 3 of illness.
Measles IgM and IgG were positive at the sixth week of illness, indicating seroconversion following MMR immunization.
Influenza A RNA was detected in the throat swab at day 3 of illness.
Parvovirus B19 IgM was detected in serum at the sixth week with negative IgG, but clinical significance was uncertain due to insufficient day-3 sample volume.
No laboratory-confirmed human-to-human transmission was detected during contact tracing.
captured_features: Multiplex respiratory PCR (influenza A/B, coronavirus, parainfluenza, hMPV, RSV, rhinovirus, enterovirus, parechovirus, bocavirus, adenovirus, Mycoplasma pneumoniae)
population: A single 9-month-old immunocompetent boy in Sri Lanka in the post-measles-elimination period
limitations: Single case report with no generated or analyzed dataset, limiting generalizability.
Insufficient sample volume prevented day-3 parvovirus B19 testing, and the clinical significance of parvovirus B19 IgM required wider evidence.
Resource-limited setting with reliance on clinical correlation for interpretation.
data_availability_statement: Data sharing not applicable to this article as no datasets were generated or analyzed during the current study.
